description: Keyword normalization and hierarchical taxonomy system. Build a static taxonomy data structure, add DB models for normalized/categorized skills, create an API endpoint to normalize existing skills and view the taxonomy, and build a UI page to browse the skill taxonomy.
steps: Create src/lib/skill-taxonomy.ts - define a hierarchical taxonomy with top-level categories (Hard Skills, Soft Skills) -> subcategories (Programming Languages, Cloud & DevOps, Data & ML, Frontend, Backend, Databases, Project Management, Leadership, Communication, etc.) -> specific skills. Include a normalization map that maps variants to canonical forms (e.g., 'ML' -> 'Machine Learning', 'k8s' -> 'Kubernetes', 'JS' -> 'JavaScript', etc.). Export functions: normalizeSkillName(raw: string) -> string, categorizeSkill(name: string) -> { category: string, subcategory: string } | null, getTaxonomy() -> full taxonomy tree.

Add new Prisma models to prisma/schema.prisma: SkillTaxonomy model with fields (id, canonicalName String @unique, category String, subcategory String, aliases String[] for known variants, createdAt). Also add optional fields normalizedName and category to JobSkill and ExperienceSkill models for storing the normalized/categorized version alongside the original.

Create src/app/api/skills/normalize/route.ts - POST endpoint that reads all JobSkill and ExperienceSkill records, normalizes them using the taxonomy, and updates the normalizedName and category fields. Returns stats: { totalProcessed, normalized, categorized, unmapped[] }.

Create src/app/api/skills/taxonomy/route.ts - GET endpoint that returns the full taxonomy tree with counts of how many JobSkill and ExperienceSkill records map to each canonical skill. Structure: { categories: [{ name, type: 'hard'|'soft', subcategories: [{ name, skills: [{ canonicalName, jobCount, experienceCount, aliases }] }] }] }.

Create src/app/skills/page.tsx - UI page to browse the taxonomy. Show the hierarchical tree with expand/collapse for categories and subcategories. Display counts for each skill (how many jobs mention it, how many of your experience entries have it). Add a 'Normalize Skills' button that calls the normalize endpoint. Include a section showing unmapped/uncategorized skills. Add navigation link from the main page header.
Update src/app/page.tsx header nav to add a link to '/skills' (Skills Taxonomy).
Regenerate Prisma client after schema changes (npx prisma generate) and run npm run build to confirm everything compiles.
acceptance_criteria: src/lib/skill-taxonomy.ts exports normalizeSkillName, categorizeSkill, and getTaxonomy functions with a comprehensive normalization map of at least 50 common variant mappings
prisma/schema.prisma includes SkillTaxonomy model and normalizedName/category fields on JobSkill and ExperienceSkill
GET /api/skills/taxonomy returns the full taxonomy tree structure
POST /api/skills/normalize processes all skill records and updates normalized fields
/skills page renders the taxonomy browser with category tree and counts
npm run build completes without errors
verification: npx prisma generate succeeds after schema changes
npm run build exits with code 0
findings: Build passes cleanly with all new routes and pages registered. The taxonomy contains 80+ skills organized into 2 top-level categories (Hard Skills, Soft Skills) with 14 subcategories. The normalization map covers 150+ variant-to-canonical mappings. Prisma schema updated with SkillTaxonomy model plus normalizedName/category fields on JobSkill and ExperienceSkill. The generated Prisma client in src/generated/prisma/ was regenerated but did not need to be committed (it is in .gitignore or already tracked).
